content.title: About
content.content: A taco is a Mexican dish consisting of a corn tortilla filled with chicken, beans, and cheese. The whole‑grain corn tortilla provides a light base, while the chicken, beans, and cheese make the dish hearty and nutritious.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tacos are traditionally served in small portions, allowing you to try several different fillings.
Corn tortillas have been used in Mexico for over 3,000 years.
Beans in tacos are a good source of plant protein and fiber.
The cheese commonly used is cheddar or queso fresco, which melts easily.
Typical toppings include salsa, guacamole, and a squeeze of lime.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken and beans provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Beans and whole‑grain corn tortilla supply dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Cheese adds calcium, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Using lean chicken and moderate cheese keeps saturated fat levels modest.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken and beans are sources of vitamin B6 and folate, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared sauces and cheese can be high in sodium; those with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Tacos can be calorie‑dense, especially with generous cheese and sauces; portion control is advised.

items.title: Food‑borne bacteria
items.content: Chicken must be fully cooked to avoid the risk of salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Warm the tortilla, fold it in half with the filling, and add fresh salsa, guacamole, sour cream, or lime to taste. For a lighter version, use whole‑grain tortillas and reduce the amount of cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Tacos are best eaten immediately. If needed, store them in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Keep tortillas dry in a cool place, and store raw ingredients (chicken, beans) in the fridge at ≤ 4 °C.
